tei:titleStmt.tei:title: [Gebet] Am Thora-Freudenfest
[A prayer] on Simḥat Torah, by Fanny Neuda (1855)

tei:lg.tei:l: “God’s laws bring joy to the heart.” (Psalms 19:9)

Today we celebrate a great feast of joy, the holy feast of faith and divine teaching. With joy and love we listen to the final words with which the Holy Torah addresses us; with joy and love we welcome it as it opens up to us anew today. It is the Torah that enriches us so abundantly with the joys of God, that makes us so truly happy. It is the Tree of Life, whose fruits nourish the immortal spirit and delight the devout soul; it is the standard around which all the devout gather and all those strong in faith join hands in holy covenant; it is the banner to which they swear to accomplish what is good and holy, to the glory of God and the exaltation of their faith; it is the banner they follow throughout their earthly pilgrimage; it is the chalice from which we drink quiet peace and God’s peace for the deeply troubled heart, joyful hope and sweet faith for the anxious and despondent mind, heavenly comfort and the balm of life for the soul wounded by sorrow; it is the sun that illuminates the dark valley of the earth for us; it is the light that transfigures the gloomy hut of misery and adversity and makes it shine with pure joy in God.

Thanks, praise, and glory to you, Most High, for entrusting such a treasure to us. Glory and worship to you for making our lives so rich and meaningful through your Word and your teaching. Without them, our lives would be nothing more than a desolate, fearful dream—a bridge without a railing, a boat without a guide on a stormy sea.

Oh, I feel dizzy when I consider what I would be without it, and holy joy fills my soul when I think of what I possess in it. Grant, Almighty One, that Your divine Word may always live within me, ennoble my heart, and make it strong—strong in faith, strong in love and faithfulness to You, strong in enduring and bearing Your trials and providences. May the blessing of Your teaching never depart from my home, from my children, or from my children’s children; may the bright ray of Your divine peace and Your divine joy always enlighten and transform us. Amen.
